reason: the audit ROW is advisory: it scores and prints, and branch_audit keeps it out of the gating average - a checker that moved in one commit put 17 of 18 branches red on 2026-09-13. Gating happens in the per-file CI ratchet below, which holds only the two files a clean checkout can see, and only where the fleet is already under.
design: DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593, boardroom thread 16 (converged 2026-09-15), seedgo comment 57

corpus.detail: README.md, .aipass/aipass_local_prompt.md, .trinity/{local,observations,passport}.json, DASHBOARD.local.json - apps/ is never opened

README.md.ruled: 2026-09-15 16:02 - 'readme 10k and off from start up' (DPLAN-0347 Design Decisions, README cap = RULED)
README.md.note: The boardroom proposed 6,000 and FPLAN-0593 still says 6,000 at lines 179 and 221; those lines are STALE. 10,000 is the ruling and this key is the number the audit reads.
README.md.ratchet: GATED since 2026-09-15. startup_ratchet reads THIS key at run time on every CI run - no copy of 10,000 exists in Python or in .github/. Move this number and the gate moves with it.

docs/*.md.ruled: DPLAN-0347 - every docs/ page under 20,000 chars; DPLAN-0351 (2026-09-19 09:48) put it in the audit
docs/*.md.scored_by: aipass_standards/docs_page_check reads THIS key through startup_budget_check.docs_page_cap() on every call - no copy of 20,000 exists in the checker. A page AT the cap passes; over is >.

ratchet.runs_in: .github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py (seedgo-audit job), ahead of the standards audit and over the same branch list
ratchet.boundary: chars <= cap passes; OVER is strictly greater. A file measuring exactly its cap is not a failure.
ratchet.units: chars (wc -m): decode utf-8, len(text). Never bytes, never lines, never tokens.
ratchet.why_not_gated: .trinity/ and DASHBOARD.local.json are gitignored, so a CI checkout holds none of them - a gate on them would measure nothing on every run and pass by accident forever. docs/ pages are measured by the advisory lane but not gated: the fleet holds pages that predate the 20,000-chars-per-page rule. A ratchet drops only where the corpus is already under.
ratchet.unreadable_cap: RED, naming the owner. There is no fallback constant anywhere in the gate; a cap that cannot be read means the gate has stopped measuring, and it says so instead of printing green.
ratchet.failure_line: FAIL <path> - measured <chars>, cap <cap>, owner @<branch> (<where the cap lives>)
